feedback: Integration notes for this candidate, written before it races. The controller is unchanged from the iteration 0 baseline (kp 2.0, kd 0.2, ki 0, base_speed 1.4, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]), because the Builder's change is the only variable I want to test. The main thing I had to check is that 18 mm spacing with a 16 mm footprint still gives a smooth signal. Sensors overlap, so the tape edge crosses boundaries less abruptly. Iteration 0 evidence: all 60 trials went off_track at max_error about 0.061 m with rms_error only 0.023 to 0.030 m, and line_loss_events were 1 to 2 per run, so line loss at large offsets is the dominant failure. Interpret the next race as follows. If line_loss_events drop to 0 or 1 and max_error falls below 0.06 m, keep the 72 mm span and try the next lever, the lead, by testing y = 0.02 m with the same span. If line_loss_events stay at 1 or more while max_error still reaches 0.06 m, the sensors are still losing the line, so widen to ±0.040 m, or keep the span and move back to 12 mm footprints to sharpen the edge. If line_loss is zero but max_error still reaches 0.06 m, the cause is turn authority, not sensing, so narrow the wheel track to 0.08 m or reduce mass to 0.6 kg.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stay at 1 or more on the s-bend or slalom, widen the sensor span to x = ±0.040 m (keeping 5 sensors and 16 mm footprints) to keep the tape in view at the 0.06 m offset seen in iteration 0.

If line_loss_events reach 0 but max_error still reaches about 0.06 m on the tightest bend, narrow wheel_track to 0.08 m or reduce mass to 0.6 kg, since iteration 0 showed the robot falls off with the line still visible.

If the robot completes with low max_error, test sensor_size 0.012 at the same 72 mm span to check whether 16 mm footprints blur the edge and raise steering_oscillation, since the widened footprint is untested.
